A 403 CSRF failure on hx-post after moving the form into a partial usually means the request isn't carrying the token anymore. Common causes are that the partial's form lacks `{% csrf_token %}` (having it in the base template doesn't cover a form that is swapped in), or that the partial is rendered without the request so the tag outputs nothing. A global fix is `hx-headers` on the body sending `X-CSRFToken`.
Action: I'd look at the partial and the view that renders it, check the rendered HTML for the csrfmiddlewaretoken field, and then add the tag or the body-level hx-headers; can you paste the partial?

With htmx the token isn't sent automatically: a `hx-post` request only carries the CSRF token if it's in the form that gets posted or in a header. Most likely the partial's form no longer contains `{% csrf_token %}`, or you render the partial without the request so the token is empty. Fixes: put `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form, or set `hx-headers='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'` on the body in the base template.
Action: ask you to paste the partial and the view that renders it, so I can tell which of those it is.

Most likely the token no longer reaches the request. With htmx the CSRF token has to be sent with the POST, either from a `{% csrf_token %}` inside the form or via an `X-CSRFToken` header (often set with `hx-headers` on body). Moving the form into a partial can break that, for instance if the partial is rendered without the request so the tag outputs nothing, or if the header lives on an element the partial no longer sits under.
Action: look at the partial and the view that renders it, check the posted request in dev tools for the token, and fix accordingly.
